text:
Maya (CEO): Opening a short follow-up from today's all-hands. Drop quick clarifying Qs about mission, positioning, and competitor messaging. I'll answer or assign. :wave:

Priya (Head of Product): For product pages: should we lead with developer experience or enterprise controls first?

Maya (CEO): Lead with developer experience for PLG flows, but have a clear enterprise callout: Private + KMS + SLA. Two-line hero works best.

Jon (CTO): For engineering demos: always show a measurable trade-off (latency vs cost) not just text output. Numbers build trust.

Ravi (Solutions): Field ask: prospects ask "why Redwood vs model-zoo vendors?" Short rebuttal?

Maya (CEO): Say: model choice matters, but most customers fail at serving. We deliver predictable SLOs, cost controls, and deployment modes that match risk profiles.

Casey (Sales): Need a one-liner for decks that calls out Private + SLA + KMS succinctly.

Maya (CEO): Draft: "Redwood Inference: unified runtime — hosted, dedicated, or private — with enterprise SLAs and KMS integrations." Trim as needed.

DesignBot: Uploaded hero comps to the drive: https://redwood.internal/design/all-hands-hero-2300

Priya (Head of Product): Roadmap prioritization question: kernel perf vs rollout tooling this quarter?

Jon (CTO): Kernel perf for Dedicated users first, rollout/canary tooling to increase PLG conversion. Triage by customer impact signals.

Ravi (Solutions): Sales trigger check: what metric moves a lead to sales outreach?

Priya (Head of Product): Current trigger: sustained >$5k/mo, repeated p95 breaches, or explicit compliance needs. I'll formalize the playbook.

Maya (CEO): Action items: Priya publish the playbook draft, Jon share demo snippets for slides, Design to finalize hero copy. I'll follow up with Legal on safe performance lines. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
